deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues §3 of a short manuscript on products and series built from cubes. On the previous page Ramanujan stated (9), Binet's second formula for log Gamma. He then derived (10): (1/2)log(2πα) + log P(α) = log((cosh(πα√3) − cos(πα))/(πα)) − πα/√3 + 2∫_0^∞ arctan((x/α)^3)/(e^{2πx}−1) dx, where P(α) = ∏_{n≥1}(1+α^3/n^3).

PART A (end of §3): evaluating J_α = ∫_0^∞ arctan(x^3)/(e^{2παx}−1) dx.
- [mine] Substituting x = αt in (10) gives J_α = (1/(2α))[(1/2)log(2πα) + log P(α) − log((cosh πα√3 − cos πα)/(πα)) + πα/√3].
- [mine] Factor 1+α^3/n^3 = (1+α/n)(1−αe^{iπ/3}/n)(1−αe^{−iπ/3}/n). The linear terms cancel, so P(α) = 1/(Γ(1+α)|Γ(1−αe^{iπ/3})|^2).
- For integer α, 1−αe^{iπ/3} has real part 1/2 or an integer. The reflection formulas |Γ(1/2+iy)|^2 = π/cosh(πy) and |Γ(1+iy)|^2 = πy/sinh(πy) then make P(α) elementary. Hence J_α is 'finite' for every positive integer α, as stated.
- α=1 [mine]: P(1) = cosh(π√3/2)/π and cosh(π√3)+1 = 2cosh^2(π√3/2). Using log cosh c = c + log(1+e^{−2c}) − log 2, one gets J_1 = (1/4)log 2π − (1/2)log(1+e^{−π√3}) − π/(4√3), as on the page.
- α=2 [mine]: 1−2e^{iπ/3} = −i√3, so P(2) = √3 sinh(π√3)/(2π). Also cosh 2π√3 − 1 = 2sinh^2(π√3). Together these give J_2 = (1/8)log 12π − (1/4)log(1−e^{−2π√3}) − π/(4√3), as on the page.

PART B (§4, formula (11)): S(α) = Σ_{n≥1}(−1)^{n−1} n^2/(n^3+α^3).
- [mine] The roots of n^3 = −α^3 are −α and αe^{±iπ/3}. Hence n^2/(n^3+α^3) = (1/3)[1/(n+α) + 1/(n−αe^{iπ/3}) + 1/(n−αe^{−iπ/3})].
- The conjugate pair combines to 4(2n−α)/((2n−α)^2+3α^2). This gives (11): S = (1/3)Σ(−1)^{n−1}/(n+α) + (4/3)Σ(−1)^{n−1}(2n−α)/((2n−α)^2+3α^2).
- Classical identity used: Σ_{k≥0}(−1)^k(2k+1)/((2k+1)^2+x^2) = (π/4)sech(πx/2).
- For odd α, 2n−α runs over odd integers, so after a finite reindexing the second series becomes (π/4)sech(πα√3/2) plus rational terms. The first series becomes ±log 2 plus rational terms.
- α=1: (1/3)(1−log 2) + (4/3)(π/4)sech(π√3/2). Thus Σ(−1)^{n−1}n^2/(n^3+1) = (1/3)(1 − log 2 + π sech(π√3/2)).

PART C (formula (12)): I(α) = ∫_0^∞ x^5/(sinh(πx)(α^6+x^6)) dx for α>0.
- Uses the partial-fraction expansion π/sinh(πx) = 1/x + 2xΣ_{n≥1}(−1)^n/(x^2+n^2). Hence x^5/sinh(πx) = (2/π)x^6{1/(2x^2) + Σ(−1)^n/(n^2+x^2)}, which is the first line of (12).
- [mine] Integrate term by term with b_k = αe^{iπk/3}, k = 0, ±1 (the roots of b^6 = α^6 with Re b > 0).
  - Write x^6/(x^6+α^6) = 1 − Σ_k (b_k^2/3)/(x^2+b_k^2).
  - Use (2/π)∫_0^∞ dx/((x^2+n^2)(x^2+b^2)) = 1/(nb(n+b)).
  - Then (2/π)∫_0^∞ x^6 dx/((n^2+x^2)(α^6+x^6)) = (1/3)Σ_k 1/(n+b_k) = (1/3)[1/(n+α) + 4(2n+α)/((2n+α)^2+3α^2)].
  - The n=0 term is (1/π)∫x^4/(α^6+x^6)dx = 1/(3α).
- Summing with signs (−1)^n gives the stated (12).
- α=1: the first series is (1/3)log 2. The second series is −(4/3)[3/12 − 5/28 + ...] = −(4/3)(1/4 − (π/4)sech(π√3/2)). Thus I(1) = (1/3)(log 2 − 1 + π sech(π√3/2)), as stated.

Purpose: to show that these Binet-type integrals and alternating cubic series have closed forms for integer (resp. odd) α, as corollaries of the cubic Gamma-product theory of §§1–2.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Every displayed closed form was checked: both arctan x^3 integrals symbolically via Gamma reflection; the series and integral for α=1 symbolically and numerically (J_1 ≈ 0.003855, series ≈ 0.2396, I(1) ≈ 0.0350).

Minor gaps in rigour: the term-by-term integration in (12) involves a conditionally convergent alternating series and needs justification (dominated/Abel argument). For odd α>1 the 'finite terms' claim requires reindexing finitely many terms where 2n−α<0. Ramanujan leaves both implicit.

results.what: ∫_0^∞ arctan(x^3)/(e^{2παx}−1)dx is elementary for positive integer α. Explicit values: α=1 gives (1/4)log2π − (1/2)log(1+e^{−π√3}) − π/(4√3); α=2 gives (1/8)log12π − (1/4)log(1−e^{−2π√3}) − π/(4√3).
results.modern_name: Binet's second formula applied to cubic Gamma products; evaluation via the reflection formula

results.what: Partial-fraction identity (11) for Σ(−1)^{n−1}n^2/(n^3+α^3), and its evaluation for odd α, e.g. α=1 gives (1/3)(1−log2+π sech(π√3/2)).
results.modern_name: Partial fractions plus the classical sech series (Mittag-Leffler expansion)
results.usually_credited_to: Classical method; this specific evaluation is Ramanujan's (studied by Andrews–Berndt in the edition of this manuscript)

results.what: Integral (12): ∫_0^∞ x^5/(sinh πx (α^6+x^6))dx as the analogous series, with closed form for odd α, e.g. α=1 gives (1/3)(log2−1+π sech(π√3/2)).
results.modern_name: Integral evaluated by the Mittag-Leffler expansion of csch

deep.surprise_reason: These are elegant but elementary consequences of Gamma reflection and partial fractions. The manuscript is known: it is linked to Ramanujan's 1915 JIMS paper on ∏[1+(x/(a+nd))^3] and to the unpublished manuscript edited by Berndt and in Andrews–Berndt, Lost Notebook Part IV. Nothing here anticipates later work.

checkable.asserts: P(2) used for the α=2 integral
P(1) used for the α=1 integral
